dedupe_keys.name: divvy bike share trip history data chicago

description: Divvy, the bike-sharing system of Chicago, publishes its historical trip data for public use. Each trip is anonymised and includes the start and end day and time, the start and end station and the rider type (member, single ride or day pass). Trips taken by staff while servicing and inspecting the system and trips shorter than 60 seconds, likely false starts or re-docking, are removed. The data are released monthly, and live station information is available in a GBFS JSON feed. The site is run by Lyft, the system's operator. Coverage: the Divvy system in Chicago. Format and access: downloadable monthly trip files and a real-time GBFS feed, without registration. Licence and cost: free under the Divvy Data License Agreement. Caveats: station-based trips only, with rider type but no demographics, and cleaning rules remove some short trips. It supports capacity planning, demand modelling and agent-based studies of bike sharing and active travel. It complements the Citi Bike system data, the GBFS specification and the Chicago traffic tracker records in the catalogue.
